Something happens after certain infections, and it keeps happening the same way, no matter which infection triggers it. When people survive infections like SARS-CoV-2, the Ebola virus, dengue fever, or the bacterium that causes Lyme disease, a fraction of them go on to develop chronic symptoms that persist for months or years, and those symptoms look strikingly similar across very different infections. In 2024 the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, a research body that advises the U.S. government, grouped these post-infection illnesses under one umbrella term: infection-associated chronic illness, or I-A-C-I for short. This video walks through what that umbrella covers, why researchers grouped it that way, and what's actually established versus still being tested.
